To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the strange form factors are zero within the experimental uncertainties.

the HAPPEX collaboration has measured the parity-violating asymmetry in the elastic scattering of polarized electrons from protons at a beam energy of 3.34 GeV and an angle of 12 degrees to a precision of +/- 0.15% of the asymmetry.

the HAPPEX collaboration has performed the first parity violating elastic electron scattering experiment at a high energy electron accelerator and that this measurement has been carried out with a precision of 10-5.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the nucleons.

the search for new physics beyond the Standard Model of particle physics, in this case, the existence of a new force between quarks mediated by the exchange of a new neutral particle, a strange quark.
the study of the structure of the nucleons, and in particular the role of the strange quark in the proton and neutron structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HAPPEX has demonstrated the feasibility of a new experimental technique and has provided a first measurement which is consistent with theoretical expectations.
there is no evidence for strange quark form factor contributions to the proton elastic scattering at this momentum and scattering angle.

the HAPPEX collaboration did not detect any evidence for a contribution of the strange quark vector form factors to the proton elastic scattering cross section at Q2 = 0.48 GeV2 and theta = 12.5 deg, and the data are consistent with the hypothesis that the strange quark contribution to the proton vector form factors is zero.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strange quark contributions to the electromagnetic nucleon form factors at the momentum transfer of Q = 0.47 GeV are consistent with zero.
the first experiment of a new program to study the strange structure of hadrons has been completed and has shown that the strange quark contribution to the nucleon is consistent with zero.
we have demonstrated that parity violation in the elastic scattering of electrons from protons can be measured with sufficient precision to probe the strange form factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have established that the HAPPEX technique can measure the strange form factors to the required precision.
it is possible to measure the strange form factor with high precision at a future parity violating electron scattering experiment.
it is now possible to probe the strange quark structure of the nucleons via parity violating electron elastic scattering.
